speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: asked	the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources with regard to the increasing number of dengue cases (a) whether current enforcement and fines are sufficient to deter owners of properties that are breeding grounds; and (b) what financial and resource support are provided for research to combat and reduce the Aedes mosquito population.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This increase may be due in part to the change in the main circulating dengue serotype.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We have also observed an increase in the Aedes mosquito population.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The warmer-than-usual year-end weather due to the El Nino phenomenon has aided the breeding and spread of both Aedes mosquitoes and the dengue virus in Singapore and in the region.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Source reduction remains the most effective way to curtail the transmission of dengue.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In anticipation of a rise in dengue cases, the National Environment Agency (NEA), together with members of the Inter-Agency Dengue Task Force, has stepped up source reduction efforts earlier than usual.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: NEA has also stepped-up publicity efforts to raise awareness of the "Five-Step Mozzie Wipeout" and encourage the community to take part actively to prevent dengue.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Owners of premises in dengue clusters found with breeding habitats can be fined up to $5,000 under the Control of Vectors and Pesticides Act.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The current penalties have been effective in keeping re-offending rates low.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Nonetheless, my Ministry will continue to monitor the situation and introduce stiffer penalties if necessary.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Besides checking homes, NEA has also intensified checks for other areas, including construction sites, and taken stern action against those found breeding mosquitoes.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In 2015, more than 900 Notices to Attend Court were issued to construction site contractors and over 100 Court prosecutions were taken against contractors for repeat offences.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In the same period, more than 100 Stop Work Orders have been issued to construction sites to ensure that proper mosquito control measures were put in place before construction was allowed to resume.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: My Ministry has set aside about $2.5 million each year to conduct multidisciplinary research in controlling the mosquito population, for example, for the development of surveillance and control tools such as Gravitraps.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The Government is also tracking the development of the dengue vaccine, Dengvaxia, and will carefully evaluate the vaccine to ensure that it is safe, of high quality and effective before it is made available in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As a community, we need to continue to play our part to remove potential breeding habitats from places under our care.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is the most effective way to control mosquito breeding.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: My Ministry will also continue to work with our partners to keep up our fight against dengue through a combination of surveillance, public education, enforcement, source reduction, as well as research into new methods of mosquito reduction.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: With the reported outbreak of Zika, which is transmitted through mosquitos, may I know what are the measures that have been taken, and what other steps can the Ministry take to help Singaporeans and to prevent this disease from spreading in Singapore?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We are equally worried about the possible detection of Zika in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: To facilitate this, the Ministry of Health (MOH) is working with NEA to enhance ongoing laboratory surveillance of sample Zika infection.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Already, Zika is a notifiable disease under the Infectious Diseases Act.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: However, having said that, the Zika virus is also transmitted by the same type of mosquito that transmits dengue.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Therefore, whatever we do for dengue, if we are effective, will also be effective to prevent Zika from spreading.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: What we are working on is that in the event that Zika were to be found in Singapore, even a single imported Zika or a local Zika case, NEA will then start to step up its vector control activities around the case's residence and/or the workplace.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: If it were a single local case, we will also conduct a vector control in the case's contacts' residences.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But beyond that, I think it is important for all of us to play our part to understand about the dengue-spreading mosquito and the real impact of how we can reduce this threat; and to understand that, in just a week, an egg can hatch into an adult mosquito and, within three weeks, the same mosquito, if it is female, will start laying 300 eggs.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: That is how it starts to spread virulently.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Therefore, we ask everybody to go out, help do something within your homes, stop its breeding, do the "Five-Step Mozzie Wipeout" and, if we are effective in this, we can also prevent Zika from spreading, if it should come to Singapore.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: What was the outcome of the dengue vaccine which was on trial in Tan Tock Seng Hospital and whether there are now enough safety studies done for us to administer this vaccine more widely?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Unfortunately, this area is under MOH and I do not have the details to be able to answer the question.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: If the Member is keen to know the answer, the Member could file a Parliamentary Question on that to MOH.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: First and foremost, the Minister alluded to the fact that the majority of the cases are in the homes.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I think the challenge is that in the residents' perception, most of the time, it comes from outside.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: So, what proportion, based on breeding sites, in any area has the Ministry found where dengue breeding is in the homes, compared to the external areas?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The Minister also mentioned that there is research being done to use male dengue mosquitos, for example, to control and curb this virulent spread.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: What safeguards are in place to ensure that when we do these biomedical, genetic modifications that they do not mutate to something else and cause other issues, even Zika?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: That is because we give them a stern warning for the first instance of discovery.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: What we have found is that if we enforce against the recalcitrant – that means having found and given a warning, we still find it again, and we impose a penalty on them – then the recurrence of finding breading in that home disappears, almost disappears.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Unfortunately, not everybody has taken a chance, but when given a penalty, that habit of checking on these things suddenly becomes much better.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: On the Wolbachia, we have been looking at this since 2005.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: And this has been confirmed by the Genetic Modification Advisory Committee in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So, the Member can rest assured that it is not a GM-mosquito.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But what we are trying to do is to use the male Aedes aegypti which will Wolbachia-carrying, to introduce that and compete with the wild-type males for the wild-type females.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Because what the scientists have discovered is that when the eggs are laid, they do not hatch.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Although promising, this is something we still need to study further, and to continue to look at what the field experience is like in other countries as they experiment on this, and to ensure that when we do this in Singapore, the impact on environment and health, and even how it affects other insects or population is not adverse.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I have one supplementary question for the Minister concerning source eradication.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: We have some residents living in private estates who may be living adjacent or near to private land which is unoccupied.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Part of our effort is to not just be reactive but to be proactive at the start or before the advent of the dengue season.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So, like I mentioned just now, we have made a lot of inspections.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In addition to the inspections, we put in what we call "Gravitraps" to monitor whether mosquitos are breeding in that area, to look at the density of the breeding, as well as the people who get infected, from their blood, to understand the serotype changes, be able to map and, therefore, to be able to look at what are the possible risks that can be prevented both to the areas as well as to the country.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Should that then appear to be something very risky, then we will deploy our resources to the appropriate places and make sure that the population comes together to make sure that they, too, will take the steps to make sure their homes are not breeding mosquitos.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For those homes which we could not get access into, we will put a notice on their doors	 because we do not know why they are not there.
